findings.title: Write lock held across file/network I/O serializes all concurrent requests
findings.body: After the fast path misses, GetWebAssets acquires entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() and holds it (via defer) across readWebAssetsFromFile / readWebAssetsFromCDN, i.e. across disk I/O and potentially an HTTP request using http.DefaultClient, which has no timeout. Whenever the cache is not populated — every call in Dev mode, and every call in non-Dev mode when the manifest is missing or unreadable (the error path leaves the cache nil, so the fast path never hits) — all concurrent goroutines calling GetWebAssets are serialized behind a single I/O operation. A slow or hung read blocks every HTTP request that needs web assets. The lock should only guard access to the cache variable; the load should happen outside the critical section (e.g. load first, then lock briefly to store, or use sync.Once/singleflight for the cold-start case).

findings.title: No re-check of cache after acquiring write lock causes duplicate loads
findings.body: The function reads the cache under RLock, releases it, then acquires the write Lock without re-checking whether entryPointAssetsCache was populated in the meantime. On a cold start in non-Dev mode, N concurrent callers all miss the fast path and each performs the full manifest read (file I/O, and CDN fetch once that path is enabled), with each one overwriting the cache. A simple `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }` re-check after acquiring the write lock would avoid the redundant work.
